resources.string: Draws the sounds you can\'t see right on your screen.\nFrom gaming to movies, try a whole new experience.
No sound is reaching the visualizer, so nothing can be drawn. The app you\'re using may not allow its sound to be shared (protected video works this way), or its own sound may be muted.
Sound type detection isn\'t working, so every sound is shown in the ambient color and vibration alerts are off. Try turning the visualizer off and on again.
Turn it on or off from the notification shade, right over your game or video.
Pull down the notification shade, tap Edit (pencil) and add “Sound visualizer” to turn it on or off right over your game or video.

Sounds are drawn on top of your game or video, so Android needs this permission. If Settings shows a list of apps, find SoundVisualizer and turn its switch on, then come back. It keeps going from there on its own.
Microphone (audio recording) permission is required to capture audio.
Android requires the microphone permission to capture sound playing on your phone. Sounds around you are not recorded.

Microphone permission wasn\'t granted. If the permission prompt doesn\'t appear again, tap “Open settings”, go to “Permissions” and allow “Microphone”. It\'s only used to capture sound playing on your phone. Sounds around you are not recorded.
Choose the basic shape of the graphics drawn on screen.
Keeps the graphics at a fixed size and shows loudness as opacity instead.
The size the graphics stay at.
How opaque the graphics get at the loudest sound.
Adjusts how large and full the graphics look.
Sets the radius of the center ring in Circle mode.
Higher values look bolder; lower values look fainter and more transparent.
How fast the graphics move to a new position when the sound changes direction.
How quickly the graphics react (pulse) to changes in loudness.
Adds a soft neon glow around the graphics. Note: uses extra resources.
Adds a slight delay so sound seems to spread from front to back.
Pause while the screen is off

While the screen is off, stops capturing sound, detecting sound types and vibrating to save battery, and picks up again when you turn the screen on. Turn this off to keep getting vibration alerts with the screen off.

Shows what the AI heard — the sound name it reported, how sure it was, and how long it took — in the top-left corner of the overlay, so the team can check how accurate it is. The readout is in English and is not meant for everyday use.
Sound type detection isn\'t working, so every sound is shown in the ambient color. Try turning the visualizer off and on again.
Vibration works only when this sound type is shown.
It won\'t vibrate while sound type detection isn\'t working.
This device can\'t adjust vibration strength, so it vibrates at the default strength.
Tap an option to feel a preview.
Visualizing sound. Sound type detection isn\'t working, so vibration alerts are off.
No sound is reaching the visualizer. The app you\'re using may not allow its sound to be shared, or its own sound may be muted.
Tells you when the sound visualizer turns off without you stopping it.

Sound capture ended, so graphics and vibration alerts are off. This happens when screen recording, screen sharing or casting starts, or when the system stops sound capture. If another app is recording, sharing or casting, turning it on again ends it.
Sound capture stopped because of an error, so graphics and vibration alerts are off.
Sound capture couldn\'t start, so graphics and vibration alerts are off.
Graphics couldn\'t be shown over other apps, so the visualizer turned off. Check that “Display over other apps” is allowed.
Sound visualizer turned off. Graphics and vibration alerts are off.
“Display over other apps” permission is required. Tap “Start” in the app to allow it.
Allow the permissions. Android asks for screen recording consent every time you turn it on.
Open a game or video, and sounds are drawn along the edges of the screen.
To turn it off, tap “Stop” on Home or in the notification.
Turn on and off from the notification shade
Tap “Add to Quick Settings” on Home to add a “Sound visualizer” button to your notification shade. You can then turn it on or off right over your game or video without switching apps.
Tap to turn it on, and tap again to turn it off. Long-press to open this app\'s settings.
On Android 12 and earlier, open the notification shade, tap Edit (pencil) and drag “Sound visualizer” in yourself.
Needed to show graphics on top of games and videos.
Android requires this permission to capture sound playing on your phone. Sounds around you are not recorded.
Android only lets apps capture your phone\'s sound through this consent. Your screen is not captured.

Shows the running notification with a Stop button, and tells you when the visualizer turns off without you stopping it. The app still works if you deny it. If it then turns off, only the vibration tells you, and Home shows what turned off when you open the app.
The whole edge of the screen pushes inward with the loudness. The side the sound comes from pushes in deeper.
Bars light up at 8 spots around the edge of the screen. Shows direction most clearly.
Draws only a thin outline of the wave, so it covers less of your game.
A ring in the center of the screen swells toward the sound.
Settings like size and opacity are saved separately for each mode and can be changed in the Settings tab.

AI sorts what you hear into ambient, speech and danger sounds. By default, ambient is white, speech is yellow and danger is red. You can change the color of each type and whether it\'s shown in the Settings tab.
When a danger sound (like a gunshot) is detected, the color changes instantly instead of fading.

Vibration alerts you even when you\'re not looking at the screen. At first only danger sounds vibrate, and you can pick a strength (Light, Medium, Strong) and pattern (Once, Twice, Long, Repeat) for each type.
Only types shown on screen vibrate. The same type won\'t vibrate again within 2 seconds, and “Repeat” vibrates every 1.5 seconds while the sound continues.
It can tell left from right, but not front from back. Graphics at the top and bottom of the screen show sounds heard equally on both sides and a sense of space.
Sounds that are identical on the left and right (mono) are shown only toward the front.

Only media and game sounds are captured. Phone calls, notification sounds and alarms are not, and apps that block audio capture (such as some video apps) can\'t be visualized. If sound is playing but nothing is drawn for about 15 seconds, Home and the running notification tell you. An app that has muted itself looks exactly the same, so we can\'t tell you which of the two it is.

Starting screen recording, screen sharing or casting turns the visualizer off, because it uses the same screen recording consent and Android lets only one app use it at a time. If another app is recording, sharing or casting, turning it on again ends it. In most cases, when it turns off without you stopping it, your phone vibrates three long times and shows a notification with a “Turn on again” button. Stopping sound capture from your phone\'s screen-sharing controls shows the same alert, and a force stop or a crash can\'t tell you at all. If notifications are off, only the vibration tells you, and Home shows what turned off when you open the app.
While the screen is off, it pauses to save battery and picks up again when you turn the screen on. You can change this under Battery in the Settings tab.
AI classification can be wrong. Don\'t rely on this app as your only safeguard when safety is at stake.
It turned off without me stopping it.

It turns off when screen recording, screen sharing or casting starts, or when sound capture stops because of an error. Tap “Turn on again” in the notification, or turn it on from Home or Quick Settings. Android asks for the screen recording consent every time, and turning it on again ends any recording, sharing or casting that is running.

Check whether the app you\'re playing blocks audio capture, and whether its own sound is turned off. If no sound reaches the visualizer for a while, Home and the running notification tell you so. Also make sure opacity isn\'t too low in Settings, and that showing the current sound type isn\'t turned off.

In Settings, under Sound types, make sure both Show and Vibrate are on for that type. While the screen is off it pauses by default, so turn off “Pause while the screen is off” under Battery in Settings to keep getting vibration alerts then. It also doesn\'t vibrate while sound type detection isn\'t working. If vibration is turned off in your phone\'s settings, it may not vibrate.
An APK built elsewhere has a different signature and can\'t be installed over the existing app. Uninstall the existing app first, then install. This resets your settings.
Does it use a lot of battery?

It only draws while there\'s sound and goes idle when it\'s quiet. While the screen is off it stops capturing sound by default. Because it keeps capturing while the screen is on, though, we recommend turning it off when you\'re not using it.
How do I change the app language?

Tap “Language” at the top of the Settings tab and pick one. “System default” follows your phone\'s language. On Android 13 and later, you can also change it under “App languages” in your phone\'s settings.
Tell us about a bug, or a sound that was shown as the wrong type. It opens GitHub in your browser with your app and device details filled in. No audio is ever sent.
No browser to open the link. Copy the device details and send them to us instead.
